note: Ad-hoc diagnostics (measured 2026-10-17 ~08:12-08:17Z) explaining the bimodal startup time. Times are spawn -> lightpanda's own first log line ($time of 'server running', which coincides with first successful TCP connect +/-1ms).
first_log_line_already_server_running: with --log-level debug the 'startup' and 'server running' lines carry the same ms timestamp; all ~58/~107ms is spent before main's first log (exec/dyld/static init/V8 platform init)

timer_coalescing_on_this_host.nanosleep_20ms_actual_ms: 40-170 (Rust thread::sleep, perl select, Atomics.wait all affected)

interpretation: Apple Silicon DVFS / cluster idle state: when the machine is otherwise idle, a fresh lightpanda process needs ~107ms to reach listen(); with one core kept busy (CPU clusters awake) ~58ms. First launch in each fresh shell is ~58ms because the shell spawn itself just woke the CPU. Not a lightpanda bug; a measurement-condition effect. Hypothesis-level explanation, consistent with the busy-spinner and taskpolicy -b experiments, not proven with powermetrics (needs sudo).
